ask: Write me a week of LinkedIn posts about hiring.

posts.content: Hiring advice I keep coming back to: write the job post for one person, not for everyone.
An interview is two people deciding whether to work together. It goes better when both of them get to ask questions.
The best hiring signal I know is still the simplest one: did they do the thing they said they would do?
A slow no is worse than a fast no. Candidates remember how long you left them waiting.
The first week matters more than the offer letter. Plan it before the person says yes.

steps.why: The decision: one call for the whole week, about one post per weekday, every item a Draft with its accounts. Never a loop of create-post. Each post is a different angle on hiring with a different first line, in the voice get-voice-context gave. Opinions only: no open roles, salaries, numbers or links, because the user gave none. If the call asks for text items, send each object JSON-encoded.
Poll until status is completed, whatever the reply's text says. Its posts are the real saved rows; report rejected and quality_blocked.

say: Saved to Acme as drafts (all 5 shown above in full). Nothing goes out yet. I kept them to opinions because you didn't name open roles or a link to apply. Schedule all 5? Or tell me what to change. Approved without a time, Bolta picks one from your posting schedule.
never: A scheduled_time or requested_action on any item.
More than 12 posts in a sitting.
An open role, number or apply link the user did not give.
